messages.author: Gustavo Seabra
messages.body:
Someone please correct me if I am wrong,  but my understanding is that AmberTools is independent of Amber. It will work just fine without Amber, and does not depend on the version of Amber installed.
On the other hand, the Amber instalation relies on the existence of AmberTools. To use the latest version of Amber, you will need to install the latest AmberTools first.
Gustavo.
--

messages.author: David A Case
messages.body:
On Sun, Jun 14, 2020, James Kress wrote:
>I do not believe AmberTools20 will work with versions of Amber prior to
>Amber20.
Just to expand: as Gustavo said, AmberTools20 can be installed, and
won't have any effect on existing versions of Amber that may be on a
machine, since they extract to different directories.
If you wish to use (say) Amber18 with AmberTools20, do this:
Install AmberTools20, and source it's "amber.sh" file: this will set
AMBERHOME to the AmberTools20 location.
Put $AMBERHOME/bin in your path, followed by /path/to/amber18/bin.
Then, when you run anything but pmemd, you will get the AmberTools20
version, and pmemd from Amber18 will also be in your PATH.  [Note that pmemd
does not depend on the AMBERHOME variable.]
....hope this helps....dac

messages.author: MYRIAN TORRES RICO
messages.body:
Hi everyone,
I have a question about the several methods in MMGBSA calculations. I
have carried out MD of 125ns in complexes carbohydrate-protein, and
next I launched over my outputs mdcrd.files MMPBSA and MMGBSA
calculations. I have read that depending the raddi bond (mbondi,
mbondi2...) the igb is different. I have used GB-OBC2 (igb=5) and I
think that it corresponding to mbondi2, but...what does it depend on
that you use igb=1, 2 or whatever?
Thanks in advance,
Myriam

messages.author: David A Case
messages.body:
On Tue, Jun 16, 2020, MYRIAN TORRES RICO wrote:
>
>I have a question about the several methods in MMGBSA calculations. I
>have carried out MD of 125ns in complexes carbohydrate-protein, and
>next I launched over my outputs mdcrd.files MMPBSA and MMGBSA
>calculations. I have read that depending the raddi bond (mbondi,
>mbondi2...) the igb is different. I have used GB-OBC2 (igb=5) and I
>think that it corresponding to mbondi2, but...what does it depend on
>that you use igb=1, 2 or whatever?
Please see Chapter 4 in the Reference Manual, which describes the
various types of gb supported with Amber.  Table 4.1 shows the radii
that are recommended for each variant.
I'm not sure I'm answering your question, though.  You might want to
look at papers that carry out similar calculations, or consult a recent
review:
%A E. Wang
%A H. Sun
%A J. Wang
%A Z. Wang
%A H. Liu
%A J.Z.H. Zhang
%A T. Hou
%T End-Point Binding Free Energy Calculation with MM/PBSA and MM/GBSA: Strategies and Applications in Drug Design
%J Chem. Rev.
%V 119
%P 9478-9508
%D 2019
...good luck....dac
